overview.text: The Hilandar Akathist icon takes its name from an Akathist being read during a fire in the monastery’s main church. It is one of several different icons called Of the Akathist.

blocks.text: The exact artwork record names this the Akathist icon of the Mother of God from Hilandar. Mary and the Child appear cheek to cheek in a Tenderness composition. The historical file is catalogued as a sixteenth-century image; that description alone does not settle every question about the panel’s restoration history.

blocks.text: The OCA places the named icon on the iconostasis of Hilandar’s katholikon, or main church. Its short life recounts the fire of 1837 and the icon’s preservation while the hymn was being read. It prints January 12 for the commemoration. The account is a received monastery tradition rather than a modern fire investigation.

blocks.text: The same official account explicitly distinguishes Hilandar’s image from the Zographou Akathist icon commemorated October 10. The shared title therefore describes a devotional association, not a single object moving between all monasteries named in such stories. The actual image and its source attribution remain attached to this entry.
